notes: The long-history ILS reference of the catalog: EUR-hedged share class, weekly NAVs since 2013-10 (748 points), so the series is the insurance risk premium itself, without the USD/EUR noise that swamps the unhedged IE000UWJUW87. Schroders' GAIA Cat Bond passed USD 4bn in 2025. Read the drawdowns as event losses, not as market beta: the asset class prices a season, not a cycle. name: Carmignac Portfolio Merger Arbitrage Plus A EUR Acc
underlying: Long the targets of publicly announced mergers, short the acquirers or an index hedge: the return is the deal spread that closes when a transaction completes, plus the collateral's cash rate
benchmark_index: active (no index; ESTR as the hurdle)
notes: Event-driven premium, structurally cash-plus: equity beta near zero (0.03 vs the S&P 500 since launch) and realized volatility around 1.5-2%, because the payoff is a spread that closes on a legal calendar rather than a market path. 'Plus' is the levered-risk version of the same book. Fees are the real objection: 1.81% management plus 0.23% transaction costs plus a 20% performance fee over the hurdle. The tail is regulatory, not macro: an antitrust block or a financing failure kills a spread instantly, and deal breaks cluster when credit tightens, so this is NOT a crisis asset. Live since 2023-04 only, in an unusually calm arbitrage regime; use MNA (2009) for a track record covering 2011, 2015-16 and 2020.

name: NYLI Merger Arbitrage ETF
underlying: IQ Merger Arbitrage Index: long the targets of announced developed-market deals, with a short global-equity index hedge
notes: The long track record of the merger-arbitrage premium (2009-11), the reason it is in the catalog: it covers the 2011 and 2015-16 deal-break waves and the 2020 shock, which no European UCITS share class does. Rules-based and cheap (0.77%) but a weaker version of the strategy than an active book: it takes the announced-deal universe wholesale, including the spreads that are wide because the deal deserves to fail. Not buyable by an EU retail investor (no PRIIPs KID): use LU2585801256 for the investable version.

name: Janus Henderson AAA CLO ETF
underlying: Actively selected AAA tranches of US collateralised loan obligations: the senior claim on a diversified pool of senior secured leveraged loans, floating-rate over SOFR
notes: The USD reference for the AAA CLO sleeve (USD 29bn, 0.20%), the long-history sibling of the euro LU2941599081. What the series shows, measured in USD: 4.4%/yr against 3.0% for T-bills (BIL) since 2020-10, for 1.6% volatility and a 2.6% worst drawdown. The spread is compensation for liquidity and complexity, not for rate duration (near zero) nor, historically, for default: no AAA CLO tranche has ever defaulted across ~7,000 tranches rated 1993-2022. The risk that does show up is mark-to-market in a liquidity squeeze, which is exactly when a retiree sells.

name: SparkChange Physical Carbon EUA ETC
underlying: EU Emission Allowances (EUAs) held physically in a Union Registry account, one allowance per unit: the permit to emit one tonne of CO2 in the EU ETS
notes: Single-commodity, not a diversified basket: the composition views count it under commodities, which is directionally right (real asset, inflation-side) but overstates its breadth. Physically backed, so no roll cost and no curve exposure, unlike futures-based carbon ETPs. The price driver is European policy (the supply of allowances is legislated down, the market stability reserve absorbs surplus), which makes the drift structural and the drawdowns political; volatility is equity-like. Held in a Union Registry account by SparkChange, listed via HANetf with a PRIIPs KID, so an EU retail investor can actually buy it (0.89%).

name: iShares EUR AAA CLO Active UCITS ETF EUR Acc

Measured against the ESTR ETF over its own window: 3.37 %/yr against 2.01 %, so +136 bp net of fees, worst drawdown 0.30 %. Read the mandate before treating it as a pure AAA sleeve: up to a fifth of the book may sit in A- or better, which is a step down the capital structure that the name does not say.

name: Invesco EUR AAA CLO UCITS ETF Acc

The whole euro AAA CLO cohort (this one, EUCL, JCL0, LAAA) lands within ten basis points of each other, which is what a spread product looks like while nothing goes wrong: the differentiators are the fee, the AA/A- allowance and the wrapper, not the manager. ALIAS: CLOAE, not CLOA. The fund's FT symbol is CLOA, but that ticker belongs to BlackRock's US iShares AAA CLO Active ETF on Nasdaq; a catalog alias would shadow it and silently answer a US question with a euro fund.

name: Fair Oaks AAA CLO Fund UCITS ETF EUR Dist
underlying: European AAA-rated CLO tranches (the EU risk-retention rule keeps most US CLOs out of a UCITS wrapper), floating rate over Euribor
notes: Europe's FIRST CLO ETF (Xetra, 2024-09-10), from the specialist Fair Oaks; EUR 37m, 0.35 %, quarterly distributions. DATA TRAP, read before comparing: the quotes are PRICE-ONLY. Yahoo carries no distribution for LAAA.DE, so the series shows 0.51 %/yr since inception where the total return is roughly three points higher (12-month distribution yield ~3.0 %). Any chart or statistic that puts this line next to an accumulating sibling (JCL0, EUCL, CLOA) understates it by the whole coupon. Prefer an accumulating share class for analysis, and keep this one for what it is, the income vehicle of the family.

name: Alternative Access First Priority CLO Bond ETF
underlying: USD first-priority (AAA) CLO tranches, floating rate over SOFR, actively selected
notes: The OLDEST genuine AAA CLO fund history available anywhere, by five weeks over JAAA: launched 2020-09-08 as the AAF First Priority CLO Bond ETF, and AAA CLO from day one, which is why it is in the catalog despite its size (USD 45m). The adviser changed twice (AXS, then Alternative Access Funds in March 2024) without a strategy change, and the calendar years read like the asset class throughout (+0.9 % in 2021, +0.1 % in 2022, +8.9 % in 2023). Small and thinly traded next to JAAA, so its tape is noisier: 3.4 % realised volatility in 2025 against 1.8 % for JAAA on the same spreads. Use JAAA as the reference series and this one to reach five weeks further back.

name: Hartford AAA CLO ETF
underlying: USD floating-rate CLO tranches rated AAA, any maturity, actively managed (since February 2024 only, see notes)
notes: HISTORY TRAP, and the reason this record exists. The quotes start in 2018 and screeners therefore advertise the longest AAA CLO track record on the market. It is a repurposed shell: the fund was the Hartford Short Duration ETF (ticker HSRT) until 2024-02-12, when objective, managers, benchmark and fee changed, and the ticker only became TRPA on 2025-04-15. The pre-2024 series is a short-duration bond fund, and it shows: -4.4 % in 2022, the year AAA CLOs returned +0.1 to +0.5 % because their coupons float. Usable as AAA CLO from February 2024 only; for anything longer use AAA (2020-09) or JAAA (2020-10).

name: Invesco Senior Loan ETF
underlying: Morningstar LSTA US Leveraged Loan 100: the hundred largest US senior secured floating-rate corporate loans, the collateral a CLO is built on
notes: The COLLATERAL of a CLO in tradable form (USD 6.7bn, 0.65 %), catalogued as the proxy for a question the CLO ETFs cannot answer: how the underlying loan market behaves across regimes. Read it as the stress the tranches sit above, never as a substitute for a CLO tranche: this is the whole loan pool, first loss included, where a AAA tranche is the senior claim on it. Drawdowns measured in USD: -24.2 % in the March 2020 liquidity panic and -7.3 % in 2022, against -2.6 % for the AAA CLO ETF (JAAA) in the same 2022 episode. Starts 2011, so it misses 2008: use OOSAX for that.

name: Invesco Senior Floating Rate Fund A
underlying: Actively managed portfolio of US senior secured floating-rate corporate loans (the CLO collateral), one of the oldest retail loan funds
benchmark_index: active (Morningstar LSTA US Leveraged Loan index as the reference)
notes: The DEEP leveraged-loan history, 1999, and the reason it is here: no CLO fund of any tranche existed before 2020, so this is the only way to see the collateral cross 2008. Total-return drawdowns in USD: -32.1 % from mid-2007 to December 2008, -21.8 % in March 2020, -6.1 % in 2022. Set against what AAA CLO tranches did in the same episodes (quoted at 70-80 % of par in 2009, then repaid in full), it gives the honest reading of the structure: the senior tranche is protected in OUTCOME, much less in PRICE during a liquidity panic. Ongoing charges are not pinned (a US class-A retail fund, load and fee schedule outside the catalog's scope); treat its level as indicative and use BKLN for anything fee-sensitive.

name: AXA Court Terme AC
underlying: Classic French money market SICAV: short-dated euro paper, the fund-form sibling of an overnight-rate ETF
notes: The DEEPEST euro cash series in the catalog, quoted since 1984, which is why a 40-year-old money fund is here at all: it shows what the short rate paid across four regimes where the ETFs only cover the last one. Measured on the mended series: +2.88 %/yr from 1999 to 2010, -0.05 %/yr from 2010 to 2022 (the negative-rate decade, when a money fund lost money after fees), +2.33 %/yr since 2022, and a worst day of -0.01 % over the whole euro era. TWO CAVEATS. The quotes run in francs until the 1999 changeover and in euros after, a 6.55957 cliff that pofo now mends automatically (the repair was missing on a first fetch until 2026-08). And the pre-1999 segment behaves like a DISTRIBUTING share class, with dozens of NAV drops too large for a money fund (down to -7 %), so it understates the total return of the franc era: treat 1999 as the start of the usable series and the earlier part as an order of magnitude.
